text:
Add setPriorities(updates: ReadonlyArray<{id:string;priority:number}>): void to PQueue, the Queue interface and PriorityQueue. Make the Queue capability optional to preserve existing custom queue types; PQueue must fall back to validated single updates when a custom queue lacks the bulk method. Validate the entire batch before any mutation: nonfinite priority -> TypeError; unknown or already-running ID -> ReferenceError. Empty batch is a no-op; duplicate IDs apply in order (last wins). Reuse single-update ordering, keep waiting-task metadata consistent, and preserve other queued tasks.

Work autonomously. Leave the final output on the main task checkout, not only a branch/worktree. You may edit production source and add tests under benchmark_tests/, but existing tests/configuration and .bench files are immutable.

what: Verified and completed the bulk `setPriorities` work. The four files already contained the full implementation; the only unfinished part was member ordering in `source/index.ts` (`#findWaitingTask`, a private method, appeared after the public `setPriority`, which root `xo` flags under `unicorn/consistent-class-member-order`). I moved that helper into the private block before the public accessors and added the required blank line between class members.

paths:
- source/queue.ts: unchanged in this session (already correct); `Queue` has optional `setPriorities?(updates: ReadonlyArray<{id: string; priority: number}>)` beside required `setPriority`.
- source/priority-queue.ts: unchanged in this session (already correct); `setPriorities` validates all priorities (finite `TypeError`) then all ids (`ReferenceError`) before mutating, then reuses `setPriority` in array order, preserving splice/FIFO behavior and last-wins duplicates.
- source/index.ts: moved `#findWaitingTask` from just after `setPriority` into the private block just after `#add` (before `timeout` accessor), with a blank line separating class members; `PQueue.setPriorities` was already complete.
- benchmark_tests/set-priorities.ts: unchanged in this session (already complete); covers empty no-op, atomic validation, non-waiting/unknown ids, reorder, duplicate last-wins, untouched FIFO, and custom-queue fallback.

facts:
- `PQueue.setPriorities` validates every `priority` first (`typeof priority !== 'number' || !Number.isFinite(priority)`), then every id via `#findWaitingTask` (waiting tasks only), so already-running/unknown ids throw `ReferenceError`, all before queue mutation.
- It then returns void for an empty batch; if `this.#queue.setPriorities` exists it calls it and assigns each update's priority back onto `waitingTask.priority` (array order, so duplicates last-wins); otherwise it falls back to `this.setPriority(id, priority)` for each update.
- `PriorityQueue.setPriorities` has the same validation order, searches only live entries with `#findIndex`, then invokes existing `setPriority`, so tie-breaking is identical to single updates.
- Final `get_diagnostics` is clean on all four files.
- `node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit` exits 0.
- Target lint `../node_modules/.bin/xo set-priorities.ts` (cwd `benchmark_tests`) exits 0.
- Target tests pass 8/8.
- Existing full test suite was run and passed 280/280 before the structural move (the move is behavior-neutral).

reasoning: The queue type keeps `setPriorities` optional so existing custom `Queue` implementations still typecheck and the PQueue public API can detect absence and fall back. Validation is split into two passes on purpose: all priorities first, then all ids, so no queue metadata or order changes when any element is invalid. Reusing existing `setPriority` inside `PriorityQueue` guarantees reorder and FIFO tie-break semantics match the single-item path exactly; applying in array order makes duplicate ids naturally last-wins. In `PQueue`, pre-validating against `#waitingTasks` rather than the concrete queue is what makes the same `ReferenceError` work for both the default and custom-queue fallback path before any mutation.

Make the Queue capability optional to preserve existing custom queue types; PQueue must fall back to validated single updates when a custom queue lacks the bulk method. Add setPriorities(updates: ReadonlyArray<{id:string;priority:number}>): void to PQueue, the Queue interface and PriorityQueue. User task:
Add setPriorities(updates: ReadonlyArray<{id:string;priority:number}>): void to PQueue, the Queue interface and PriorityQueue. Make the Queue capability optional to preserve existing custom queue types; PQueue must fall back to validated single updates when a custom queue lacks the bulk method. Reuse single-update ordering, keep waiting-task metadata consistent, and preserve other queued tasks.
